note: Reference masses and animal force figures used to translate a lifted tonnage into a picture. Every figure carries its source. Animal strength is largely folklore: entries say how well attested they are, and the app hedges accordingly.

animals.note: Animal Diversity Web (Univ. of Michigan Museum of Zoology) gives a range mass of 4.1 to 5.4 kg for the domestic cat. 4.5 kg sits in that range and matches the common vet-clinic reference for a healthy adult. Smallest anchor in the set, so early-session totals still land on a real comparison.

AKC official Bulldog breed standard: "The size for mature dogs is about 50 pounds; for mature bitches about 40 pounds." 50 lb converts to 22.7 kg; 22 kg is used as the representative adult, sitting just above the male standard's metric equivalent and comfortably above the 18 kg female figure.
Global average adult body mass is 62 kg, with North America highest at 80.7 kg. The global figure is used so the comparison reads the same for every user regardless of region.
animals.source: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/06/120618095057.htm — Walpole et al., "The weight of nations: an estimation of adult human biomass," BMC Public Health 2012

animals.note: Smithsonian's National Zoo states wild males weigh up to 250 pounds (113 kg) and females rarely reach 220 pounds (104 kg). 100 kg is a round representative adult that sits below both stated ceilings.
Animal Diversity Web gives a range mass of 90 to 130 kg for the common ostrich. 110 kg is the midpoint. Useful mid-low anchor between the panda and the gorilla.

Animal Diversity Web: "In the wild, male gorillas average 180 kg, with females often almost half that weight." The wild male average is used directly rather than the 275 kg captive maximum, which is not representative.

National Wildlife Federation: males average 200 to 300 kilograms (about 400 to 600 pounds); a large female in the lower 48 states weighs 110 to 160 kg. 250 kg is the midpoint of the stated male average range.

Animal Diversity Web: adult males weigh 300 to 800 kg (660 to 1760 lbs); females are smaller at 150 to 300 kg. 450 kg is a representative adult male, in the lower-middle of the male range rather than at the extreme.

Animal Diversity Web: live weights of males range from 360 to 600 kg, females 270 to 400 kg. 500 kg is a representative adult bull inside the stated male range. Note the plural is unchanged, so any pluralisation logic needs an exception for this entry.
a draft horse weighs about 700 kilograms

National Park Service (Yellowstone): a male (bull) weighs up to 2,000 pounds and a female (cow) up to 1,000 pounds. 900 kg is the metric equivalent of the 2,000 lb bull figure, and matches the top of the 318 to 900 kg range Animal Diversity Web lists for the species. Plural is unchanged.

Animal Diversity Web lists an average mass of 1000 kg for the walrus, with males 1200 to 1500 kg and females 600 to 850 kg. The stated species average is used unchanged, which makes this a clean round anchor at one tonne.

Animal Diversity Web gives a range mass of 1180 to 1930 kg, with females up to 1180 kg and males up to 1930 kg. 1200 kg is a representative adult near the female figure and the bottom of the species range.

Animal Diversity Web gives a range mass of 1300 to 4500 kg, noting males average roughly 200 kg more than females at maturity and that 4500 kg is the largest recorded specimen. 1500 kg is a representative adult near the low end, not the record.
Animal Diversity Web: "They weigh approximately 1000 to 3600 kg as adults," with females slightly smaller than males. 2300 kg is the midpoint of that stated adult range.

SeaWorld's killer whale physical characteristics page gives typical adult males as 3,600 to 5,400 kg (8,000 to 12,000 lb), with the largest recorded male at 10,000 kg. 4500 kg is the midpoint of the typical adult male range. Note Animal Diversity Web quotes a higher 7200 kg male average, so this is the conservative figure.

Animal Diversity Web: males range from 4,500 to 6,100 kg, females 2,000 to 3,500 kg. 6000 kg is a representative adult bull at the top of the stated male range and is the round number most users already picture. This is the headline unit for the feature.

NOAA Fisheries quick facts list adult humpbacks at up to about 40 tons (roughly 36,000 kg). 30,000 kg is used as a representative adult below that ceiling. Included specifically to fill the gap between the elephant and the blue whale so very large lifetime tonnage totals still get a sensible match.

NOAA Fisheries quick facts list blue whales at up to 330,000 pounds (about 150,000 kg), noting North Atlantic and North Pacific animals typically exceed 100,000 pounds. Whale and Dolphin Conservation independently gives adult males at 150,000 kg and females at 190,000 kg. 150,000 kg is the male figure, corroborated by both sources. Largest anchor in the set.

strength.note: a bald eagle can carry about 2.3 kilograms in flight, roughly half its own body weight
gold-rush freight teams were expected to move about 91 kilograms of load per dog
a working draft horse sustains a true pulling force of about 100 kilograms all day
the strongest chimpanzee ever measured pulled 221 kilograms, about 4.6 times its own body weight
a large elephant is reckoned to lift around 300 kilograms with its trunk alone
a grizzly has been filmed hauling an adult bull elk of roughly 318 kilograms out of a mudhole
no gorilla has ever had its strength measured; scaling the only controlled great-ape measurement to gorilla size suggests roughly 530 kilograms
strength.source: Finch, G. (1943) J. Mammalogy 24(2):224-228 (chimp Bokar, 48.5 kg, 221 kg max pull), scaled by mass^0.67. The widely repeated 815 kg figure is an unverified extrapolation.
